answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally acquired stake before it can earn reputation or access high-value tasks. Rewards accrue slowly, while proven fraud triggers slashing and a delay before the stake can be withdrawn. One operator can still create many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing that capital; copying a name is cheap, sustaining credible accounts is not. The ocean of possible personas offers no shortcut, and even a sable relic token helps only if it carries real, slashable value.
